title: More scam, than usefull
body: The application might have been created by a scientist, but its goal is not to help the user, but to rip them off for as much money as possible, as quickly as possible. Upon initial installation, the app starts a survey, supposedly to analyze and build a strategy. However, at the end, it begins suggesting improvements for certain aspects of life, and it turns out that "improvement" actually means purchasing additional services or apps. For example, the user taps "improve sleep," and money is deducted from their account to purchase a separate sleep-tracking app.

title: Fabulous scam
body: This is the least fabulous app I ever had the displeasure of using. Cluttered interface makes it near impossible to find things you want to find and the app constantly pushes you toward some generic journey it thinks you need. I don’t need to be reminded to drink water, but there’s no way to skip it (or there is but it’s somewhere deep in the constantly blinking ui). Also I understand that the 7 day trial is the way to make quick 50$, but habit changing app should have at least a month. Especially if 3 of those 7 days is spent on drinking water. It said that my trial period is until February 6, I cancelled in the morning of February 6 and was still billed for the whole year. The support hasn’t been answering for a week. In short, a scam app, would never recommend it to any of my friends. Should’ve read the other reviews of people who were scammed by the app too.
